arxiv-2011-10915.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Markov Routing Games: A New Modeling Paradigm For Dynamic Traffic Assignment Journal: Transportation Research Part C
arxiv-2011-10915.creator: Zhenyu Shou, Xu Chen, Yongjie Fu, Xuan Di
arxiv-2011-10915.description: Abstract This paper aims to develop a paradigm that models the learning behavior of intelligent agents (including but not limited to autonomous vehicles, connected and automated vehicles, or human-driven vehicles with intelligent navigation systems where human drivers follow the navigation instructions completely) with a utility-optimizing goal and the system’s equilibrating processes in a routing game among atomic selfish agents.

arxiv-2102-03064.title: “I Don’t Think So”: Summarizing Policy Disagreements for Agent Comparison
arxiv-2102-03064.creator: Yotam Amitai, Ofra Amir
arxiv-2102-03064.description: Abstract With Artificial Intelligence on the rise, human interaction with autonomous agents becomes more frequent. Effective human-agent collaboration requires users to understand the agent’s behavior, as failing to do so may cause reduced productivity, misuse or frustration. Agent strategy summarization methods are used to describe the strategy of an agent to its destined user through demonstration.

arxiv-2103-11251.title: Interpretable Machine Learning: Fundamental Principles and 10 Grand Challenges
arxiv-2103-11251.creator: Cynthia Rudin 1 , Chaofan Chen 2 , Zhi Chen 1 , Haiyang Huang 1 , Lesia Semenova 1 , and Chudi Zhong 1 1 Duke University 2 University of Maine
arxiv-2103-11251.description: Abstract Interpretability in machine learning (ML) is crucial for high stakes decisions and troubleshooting. In this work, we provide fundamental principles for interpretable ML, and dispel common misunderstandings that dilute the importance of this crucial topic. We also identify 10 technical challenge areas in interpretable machine learning and provide history and background on each problem.

arxiv-2309-02273.title: Computing Hive Plots: A Combinatorial Framework
arxiv-2309-02273.creator: Martin Nöllenburg, Markus Wallinger
arxiv-2309-02273.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Martin Nöllenburg, Markus Wallinger. Hive plots are a graph visualization style placing vertices on a set of radial axes emanating from a common center and drawing edges as smooth curves connecting their respective endpoints. In previous work on hive plots, assignment to an axis and vertex positions on each axis were determined based on selected vertex attributes and the order of axes was prespecified.

arxiv-2509-10364.title: On the semi-infinite cohomology of graded-unitary vertex algebras
arxiv-2509-10364.creator: Christopher Beem, Niklas Garner
arxiv-2509-10364.description: Abstract . Recently, the first author with A. Ardehali, M. Lemos, and L. Rastelli introduced the notion of graded unitarity for vertex algebras. This generalization of unitarity is motivated by the SCFT/VOA correspondence and introduces a novel Hilbert space structure on the state space of a large class of vertex algebras that are not unitary in the conventional sense.

arxiv-2601-07064.title: Bridging Attribution and Open-Set Detection using Graph-Augmented Instance Learning in Synthetic Speech
arxiv-2601-07064.creator: Mohd Mujtaba Akhtar, Girish, Farhan Sheth, Muskaan Singh
arxiv-2601-07064.description: Abstract We propose a unified framework for not only attributing synthetic speech to its source but also for detecting speech generated by synthesizers that were not encountered during training. This requires methods that move beyond simple detection to support both detailed forensic analysis and open-set generalization.

pmc-12634836.description: IntroductionExercise training combined with supplements may be effective in enhancing antioxidant defense and mitochondrial function. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the response of glutathione peroxidase and cytochrome c to forced resistance swimming training and sodium selenite in the heart tissue of male rats.

pmc-12773508.title: Abstract 197: Mechanical Thrombectomy Of Basilar Artery Occlusion On A Hypoplastic Vertebrobasilar Circulation
pmc-12773508.creator: Mohammad R. Ghani, Syed Zahid Ali, Ping Shi, Erik Gentry, Wei Liu
pmc-12773508.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionBasilar artery occlusion (BAO) is one of the most severe acute ischemic strokes which carries high mortality and morbidity risk. Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has been used as a promising treatment for BAO. However, the vertebral‐basilar anatomy is more challenging for MT compared to the anterior circulation due to several congenital variants such as hypoplastic vertebral artery, fenestration on the vertebrobasilar junction, or chronic asymptomatic occlusions of vertebral arteries, and tortuous subclavian arteries and vertebral arteries (VAs).

pmc-12986498.title: A Latent Autoantibody Axis Associated with Vascular Vulnerability in Ischemic Stroke: Integrated Statistical and Machine-Learning Analysis
pmc-12986498.creator: Tomohiro Sugiyama, Yoichi Yoshida, Takaki Hiwasa, Masaaki Kubota, Seiichiro Mine, Yoshinori Higuchi
pmc-12986498.description: Ischemic stroke remains a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and improved strategies for identifying individuals at elevated vascular risk are needed. Serum autoantibodies have emerged as potential biomarkers reflecting vascular injury and immune activation; however, their integrative biological significance and incremental predictive value beyond established clinical risk factors remain unclear.

pmc-13093304.title: Long‐Term Effects of Freeze–Thaw Events on Ecosystem Carbon Exchange
pmc-13093304.creator: Qingfeng Xu, Kai Guo, Jintao Zhao, Chunjing Zhao, Yinan Wang, Fengying Jin
pmc-13093304.description: Freezing–thawing cycle (FTC) event plays a significant role in the regions with relative higher altitude and latitude, which is judged based on soil temperature. It affects soil environment and ecosystem productivity by altering soil physical structure, including physicochemical properties and water phase changes.

pmc-13153246.title: Magnetite sand as a low-cost material for electromagnetic shielding and mechanical enhancement of concrete
pmc-13153246.creator: Shady H. El-Gohary, Wegdan W. El-Nadoury, Ehab A. Kholief, Ahmed S. I.Amar, Adel M. Soliman
pmc-13153246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The widespread use of electromagnetic waves in various fields, such as communications, medicine, and household use, has become a tangible reality. However, this increasing use is surrounded by concerns about the harmful effects of electromagnetic waves. In this study, samples of concrete used in buildings were prepared, and conventional sand was replaced with magnetite sand extracted from Egyptian black sand at ratios of 10, 20, 30, and 40% of the total sand content.

pmc-13170454.title: Mental health and psychosocial sequelae of fraud victimization: a systematic review
pmc-13170454.creator: Jie Bai, Mei-Hsin Ho, Hsiang-Te Sung, Chuan-Sheng Hung, Jui-Hsiu Tsai
pmc-13170454.description: Fraud victimization is an increasingly prevalent global problem that extends beyond financial loss, and encompasses substantial mental health and psychosocial harm. Deception, emotional manipulation, and perceived betrayal have been linked to anxiety, depression, shame, trust erosion, and reduced quality of life. Despite these effects, the psychological consequences of fraud victimization remain under-recognized within healthcare and victim support systems.

pmc-13220007.title: Midterm Outcomes of 3-Component Mobile-Bearing Total Ankle Arthroplasty in 124 Ankles: Influence of Preoperative Varus, Valgus, and Neutral Alignment
pmc-13220007.creator: Jung-Won Lim, Woo Sub Kim, Je-Min Im, Hong-Geun Jung
pmc-13220007.description: BackgroundThe influence of preoperative coronal alignment on outcomes after total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) remains controversial, particularly in the presence of varus or valgus deformity. This study aimed to evaluate midterm clinical and radiographic outcomes of Salto mobile-bearing TAA according to preoperative varus, neutral, and valgus alignment.
